author: ASHLEY RODRIGUEZ Keys
title: JIATF South seizes over 2 tons of cocaine - NewsBreak
text:
By ASHLEY RODRIGUEZ Keys ,
5 hours ago
The Joint Interagency Task Force South (JIATF South) announced on Monday a successful joint operation with Ecuadorian Navy, U.S. Coast Guard and the Drug Enforcement Administration conducted in the Eastern Pacific where over two tons of cocaine were seized.
The drugs were seized from three separate high-speed vessels and the operation took place about 180 nautical miles from Manta, Ecuador, according to the announcement.
Some 2,062 kilograms of cocaine were found in hidden compartments of the vessels.
The agency called the effort, “A successful joint maritime operation” between U.S. and Ecuadorian enforcement. According to JIATF South the operation was led by the Ecuadorian Navy but JIATF South played a crucial role alongside other departments.
They said the operation “struck a significant blow against drug trafficking.”
“This successful maritime interdiction operation demonstrates the united front against cartels and narcoterrorists in the Western Hemisphere. Together, we are disrupting and dismantling the illicit networks that spread terror, violence, and corruption across our region,” JIATFS said in an announcement. “This seizure highlights the strong partnership and shared commitment between Ecuador and the United States to combat drug trafficking and secure our region.”
JIATF South did not return calls or emails regarding the operation by press time.
JIATF South is based in Key West and located at Key West’s Naval Air Station.
They monitor and target illicit drug trafficking that might pose a threat to national security in air and maritime operations. They cover a certain area, which is otherwise known as the “Joint Operating Area.” JIATF South predominantly focuses efforts near the Caribbean and Central and South America.
